title: Overproduction plus slight profitable variation leads to natural selection

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Overproduction plus slight profitable variation leads to natural selection

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because more individuals of each species are born than can survive, there is a recurring struggle for existence, so any individual that varies even slightly in a way profitable to itself has a better chance of surviving and thus of being naturally selected.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As many more individuals of each species are born than can possibly survive; and as, consequently, there is a frequently recurring struggle for existence, it follows that any being, if it vary however slightly in any manner profitable to itself, under the complex and sometimes varying conditions of life, will have a better chance of surviving, and thus be _naturally selected_.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), the Introduction; section “Introduction”. Scope: all animals and plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-intro-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Standard demographic and selection analyses directly test the mechanism in many populations. Existing datasets have strong examples but cover only a small, nonrandom fraction of all organisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate lifetime reproductive success or survival as a function of a measured heritable trait under density limitation. A consistently positive selection differential for profitable variants, coupled with excess offspring mortality, supports the claim; no differential refutes it in each tested population.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Heritability and fitness are rarely measured together.

Results from monitored species cannot establish universality.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open life-history compilations can test overproduction for hundreds of plants and animals, which is only part of the syllogism. The step from a profitable slight variation to a better chance of survival is difficult to refute without an independent definition of profit, and heritability-plus-fitness tables are not in one downloadable archive. A small team could test the demographic premise quickly and would still be short of a non-circular test of the whole mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate low-density population growth and the surplus of births over replacement from matrix models and fecundity schedules, then ask whether small heritable advantages predict higher survival or reproductive success in the same populations. Persistent geometric potential with realized populations held far below it would support the overproduction premise; a general failure of slight heritable differences to predict fitness would challenge the selection step only if 'profitable' is defined independently of the fitness outcome.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Density dependence, measurement of 'slight' variation, and publication bias in selection studies all change the apparent strength of the result.

Public demographic databases rarely pair individual-level heritable differences with fitness in the same rows.

A variation that is profitable to its bearer is already defined by improved survival or reproduction, so that half of the statement is nearly analytic.
